name: Coolidge Park
description: The Northshore's riverfront front lawn, with open green space, a restored carousel, and the north landing of the Walnut Street Bridge. A natural starting point for exploring Frazier Avenue.

image.alt: Coolidge Park's open lawn and curving paths from above, with the Chattanooga Theatre Centre and Northshore beyond

name: Coolidge Park Carousel
description: A beloved antique-style carousel inside its own pavilion at Coolidge Park — a quick, classic treat for little ones between bridge walks and ice cream stops.

image.alt: Blue roof and golden horse weathervane of the Coolidge Park carousel pavilion

verification.notes: Confirm current carousel hours and ride price with Chattanooga Parks & Outdoors before launch.

name: Renaissance Park
description: A quieter riverfront park east of the Market Street Bridge with wetlands, boardwalks, and river views. Interpretive signs share the history of the site.

verification.notes: Street address not confirmed against an official source this session.

name: Frazier Avenue Shopping District
description: The Northshore's main street, lined with independent shops, galleries, cafés, and restaurants in old storefronts "between the bridges" — the Walnut Street and Market Street bridges.

name: Locals Only Gifts and Goods
description: A gift shop on Frazier Avenue stocking small-batch goods from Tennessee makers — food, art, stationery, home goods, jewelry, apparel, and curated gift boxes. This guide's sponsor.
hours: Mon–Sat 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Sun noon–6 p.m. (per store website)

image.alt: Locals Only Gifts and Goods logo

name: Clumpies Ice Cream Co.
description: A Chattanooga favorite serving creative, handcrafted ice cream flavors. A great stop while exploring the Northshore.

verification.notes: Address from a directory listing; confirm website URL and current hours.

name: In-Town Gallery
description: An artist-run cooperative gallery that has showcased local painters, potters, jewelers, and photographers on Frazier Avenue for five decades.

name: Winder Binder Books, Art & Music
description: A Northshore staple since 1994: new and used books, vinyl records, regional folk art, and pottery under one roof. Ask about their curated mystery book boxes.

verification.notes: Official website not yet confirmed.

name: AVA Gallery (Association for Visual Arts)
description: A nonprofit gallery presenting rotating exhibits by regional and emerging artists, just off the Walnut Street Bridge.

verification.notes: Most recent address source is 2021; reconfirm before launch.

name: Chattanooga Theatre Centre
description: Chattanooga's long-running community theatre, staging musicals, plays, and youth productions beside Coolidge Park.

name: Julie Darling Donuts
description: A Northshore doughnut shop frying and glazing doughnuts through the morning, with rotating seasonal specials.

name: Brewhaus
description: A Frazier Avenue bar and restaurant known for German-inspired fare and a lively patio scene.

verification.notes: Directory source only; confirm website and description with the business.

name: Taco Mamacita
description: A colorful Northshore taqueria near the foot of the Market Street Bridge, popular for tacos and margaritas.

name: River Street Deli
description: A casual Northshore deli across from Coolidge Park — handy for a picnic lunch on the lawn.

verification.notes: Source undated; confirm the deli is open.

name: Walnut Street Bridge
description: A 2,376-foot pedestrian bridge completed in 1891 and reopened for walkers and cyclists in 1993 — one of the longest pedestrian bridges in the world, linking Downtown with the Northshore.

image.alt: The blue truss Walnut Street Bridge at sunset with the Tennessee Aquarium and mountains behind

name: Tennessee Aquarium
description: Two glass-peaked buildings on the riverfront — River Journey and Ocean Journey — tracing water from Appalachian streams to the sea. A rainy-day favorite for every age.

image.alt: Aerial view of the Tennessee Aquarium's glass peaks beside the Tennessee River

verification.notes: Address confirmed (Aquarium Plaza, 1 Broad St). Confirm website and admission before launch.

name: Creative Discovery Museum
description: A hands-on children's museum downtown with exhibits for science, art, and play — built for curious kids and the grown-ups chasing them.

verification.notes: Address and website from editorial knowledge; verify before launch.

name: Hunter Museum of American Art
description: American art from the colonial era to today, housed in a 1904 mansion and dramatic modern wings perched on the bluff above the river.

image.alt: The Hunter Museum's columned historic mansion with a bronze sculpture in front

verification.notes: Address and website from editorial knowledge; verify before launch.

name: Bluff View Art District
description: A compact, European-feeling enclave on the bluff with River Gallery, an outdoor sculpture garden, a coffeehouse, and restaurants — steps from the Hunter Museum and the Walnut Street Bridge.
address: Bluff View & E 2nd St, Chattanooga, TN 37403

verification.notes: District, not a single business — confirm preferred address and official website.

name: River Gallery
description: A fine art and fine craft gallery in the Bluff View Art District, next to its riverside sculpture garden.

verification.notes: Most recent source is 2019; confirm.

name: Ross's Landing
description: The city's riverfront park and historic landing, with terraced lawns stepping down to the water, festival space, and direct access to the Tennessee Riverwalk.

image.alt: Ross's Landing riverfront lawns and pier busy with people and paddlers

name: High Point Climbing and Fitness – Downtown
description: An indoor climbing gym in the heart of downtown with bouldering, roped climbing, and a kids' climbing area — a strong rainy-day pick for active families.

verification.notes: Confirm website, minimum ages, and waiver policy.

name: Classic Arcade Pinball Museum
description: An all-you-can-play museum of vintage and modern pinball machines and classic arcade cabinets on Broad Street — one admission, unlimited play.

name: MoonPie General Store
description: MoonPies have been made in Chattanooga since 1917. This downtown shop, inside the Southern Belle Riverboat, sells every flavor plus souvenirs and nostalgic candy.

name: Tivoli Theatre
description: A restored 1920s movie palace on Broad Street hosting touring shows, concerts, and performing arts.

verification.notes: Source from 2018; confirm website and box office phone.

name: Miller Park
description: A green pocket park on Market Street in the city center, with lawn, benches, and a fountain — a good pause between downtown stops.

verification.notes: Source from 2014; park was later renovated — confirm amenities.

name: Blue Goose Hollow
description: A small riverside park on the Tennessee Riverwalk with sculptures and markers reflecting on Chattanooga's industrial heritage and urban renewal. Restrooms and parking are reported on site.

verification.notes: No official street address found — confirm with Chattanooga Parks & Outdoors.

name: Shelia M. Jennings Westside Park
description: The Westside's neighborhood park, with ballfields, tennis courts, a playground, walking paths, and a recreation center at the heart of the community.

verification.notes: Sources give 1195 and 1200 Grove St — confirm.

name: Tennessee Riverwalk – Riverfront Parkway Access
description: A Riverwalk parking and access point along Riverfront Parkway on the Westside's river edge — walk north toward Ross's Landing and downtown.

verification.notes: Parking address from TrailLink; confirm with Hamilton County / City.

name: Chattanooga Choo Choo
description: The city's 1909 Terminal Station, now a hotel and entertainment campus with restaurants, music venues, and vintage rail cars — the anchor of the Southside.

image.alt: The red and green Chattanooga Choo Choo steam locomotive on display

verification.notes: Address from editorial knowledge; confirm website before launch.

name: Station Street
description: A short, walkable entertainment street on the Choo Choo campus — built to close for concerts and street festivals, with live music venues and bars side by side.

name: Songbirds Guitar Museum
description: A museum of rare and vintage guitars on Station Street, with small stages for live music.

verification.notes: Confirm current museum hours/status and official website.

name: Chattanooga Whiskey Experimental Distillery
description: Opened in 2015 as the first legal distillery in Chattanooga in more than a century, this working micro-distillery across from the Choo Choo offers tours and tastings (21+).

verification.notes: Confirm website URL.

name: The Hot Chocolatier
description: A couple-run chocolate shop across from the Choo Choo making truffles, sipping chocolate, and pastries by hand.

verification.notes: Sources disagree: 1437 vs 1423 Market St. Confirm with the shop.

name: Niedlov's Bakery & Café
description: A Main Street bakery known for naturally leavened bread and a busy breakfast-and-lunch café counter.

name: Main Street Meats
description: A working butcher counter and restaurant on East Main Street, celebrated for its burgers and locally sourced meats.

verification.notes: Street number not confirmed by a source this session.

name: State of Confusion
description: A Main Street restaurant with Latin-leaning plates from the wood grill, a covered patio, and weekend brunch.

name: Hi-Fi Clyde's
description: A big-room Southside bar and restaurant with murals, games, and live music Thursday through Sunday. Fridays and Saturdays go 21+ after 8 p.m.

name: Main Terrain Art Park
description: A former rail corridor turned art-and-fitness park, where nine large sculptures inspired by the city's bridges double as exercise stations — and the park quietly manages stormwater, too.

name: Sculpture Fields at Montague Park
description: A sprawling outdoor sculpture park with large-scale works set along walking paths and open lawns — free, dog-friendly, and a favorite for kite flying.

image.alt: Aerial view of Sculpture Fields' winding paths and sculptures with Lookout Mountain behind

name: Finley Stadium
description: Home of UTC Mocs football and Chattanooga FC soccer, plus concerts and community events on the Southside.

image.alt: Aerial view of a full Finley Stadium during an evening soccer match

verification.notes: Street address not confirmed this session.

name: Lookout Mountain Incline Railway
description: A funicular railway dating to 1895 that climbs about a mile up Lookout Mountain from St. Elmo to the summit near Point Park. Combination tickets with other mountain attractions are available.

name: St. Elmo Historic District
description: One of Chattanooga's oldest suburbs, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, with Victorian and Craftsman homes on tree-lined streets at the foot of Lookout Mountain.

name: International Towing & Recovery Museum
description: The world's first tow truck was built in Chattanooga in 1916. This one-of-a-kind museum displays restored wreckers and antique cars, plus the moving Wall of the Fallen memorial.

name: Little Coyote
description: Texas-style smoked meats and house-made tortillas with views of Lookout Mountain; recognized with a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.

name: The Purple Daisy Picnic Cafe
description: A cheerful St. Elmo café near the Incline serving barbecue and picnic fare — save room for the bread pudding.

name: St. Elmo Mercantile
description: A neighborhood shop for curated everyday goods beside the Incline's lower station; it also houses a MoonPie General Store outpost.

name: Point Park (Chickamauga & Chattanooga National Military Park)
description: A National Park Service site atop Lookout Mountain with sweeping views of the city and Moccasin Bend, Civil War history, and the trailhead for the Bluff Trail. Entrance fee applies.
address: 110 Point Park Rd, Lookout Mountain, TN 37350

image.alt: View from Lookout Mountain over the Tennessee River's Moccasin Bend at sunrise

name: Ruby Falls
description: A guided walk deep inside Lookout Mountain to an underground waterfall, plus a scenic overlook above ground.

verification.notes: Address and website from editorial knowledge; verify before launch.

name: Rock City Gardens
description: A walking trail through giant rock formations and gardens on top of Lookout Mountain (just over the Georgia line), ending at Lover's Leap and its famous view.

image.alt: Rock City's stone cliffs and Lover's Leap overlook above the valley

verification.notes: Address and website from editorial knowledge; verify before launch.

name: Chattanooga Zoo

name: Tennessee Valley Railroad Museum

name: Ed Johnson Memorial
description: Three bronze figures by artist Jerome Meadows honor Ed Johnson, who was lynched on the Walnut Street Bridge in 1906, and his attorneys Noah Parden and Styles Hutchins. Dedicated in 2021 at the bridge's downtown end as a place of remembrance and reconciliation.
